# Session learnings and closeout log

This live, append-only file preserves what each Codex task learned before its
task, branch, or worktree is archived or pruned. It is the durable handoff layer
between short-lived execution contexts and the repository.

## The ritual

At the end of every repository task:

1. Re-read the task's actual diff, commits, test output, pull request, and merge
   state. Do not infer completion from a task title or an old status note.
2. Append one entry using the template below. Record unknowns as `Not confirmed`.
3. Commit the entry with the work when practical, or point the coordinating task
   to the exact appended entry before handoff.
4. The coordinator reconciles the entry against current `origin/main`, GitHub
   pull requests, branch ancestry or patch equivalence, worktree cleanliness,
   and task status.
5. Only after that reconciliation may the coordinator archive the task and
   remove a merged or fully superseded branch/worktree. Never force-delete an
   unconfirmed branch.

## Entry template

```markdown
### YYYY-MM-DD — Task title

- Task: `TASK_ID`
- Branch/worktree: `BRANCH` at `ABSOLUTE_PATH`
- Outcome: Completed | Merged | Superseded | Blocked | In progress
- Commits/PRs: exact SHAs and links, or `Not confirmed`
- Validation: commands/checks actually run and their result
- Durable learnings: decisions, invariants, or techniques future tasks should reuse
- Failed approaches: symptoms, causes, and the safer correction
- Remaining follow-ups: explicit open work, or `None`
```

## Prune gate

A branch/worktree/task is eligible for cleanup only when all applicable answers
are yes:

- Is the worktree clean, with no Git operation in progress?
- Is every useful commit reachable from `origin/main`, or explicitly documented
  as patch-equivalent/superseded after diff review?
- Is the pull request merged or closed with no wanted commits left behind?
- Are required checks and release evidence recorded when the work affected a
  release?
- Has the owning task added or confirmed a learning entry here?
- Is the task idle/completed rather than actively writing to the worktree?

If any answer is no or unknown, retain the item and record the exact blocker.

Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/functions-matching.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/catalog-pg-type.html .

No approved connector/runtime necessity is established by these artifacts; omit it unless the exact generated/native operation proves a need. Owner/writer separation also requires transitive membership, ADMIN/INHERIT/SET and effective-privilege checks; safe role attribute flags alone do not exclude an existing service-agent path through another login to the future owner or managed role. Fixed postconditions are presently comments immediately before COMMIT. The implementation must perform them within the transaction before committing, including effective ACLs/defaults, no upward privilege path, unchanged source-object inventory, and no initializer dependencies. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-priv.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/functions-info.html .
- PG18-consistent design, conditional on native capability: SET LOCAL ROLE makes the permanent managed role the current creator; a nonsuperuser CREATEROLE creator receives the automatic bootstrap-superuser ADMIN grant. This keeps that dependency on the permanent role rather than temporary session_user. Explicit self-grants with INHERIT/SET are allowed and may coexist with bootstrap grantor rows; do not impose a false one-row-per-role/member invariant or revoke permanent ADMIN dependencies. Membership direction from app roles down to the permanent administrator is appropriate; never grant the managed role upward to app actors. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/role-attributes.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-grant.html .
- Schema/default-ACL requirements: temporarily granting database CREATE to the new owner, transferring public schema ownership, and revoking database CREATE follows ALTER SCHEMA requirements if the executing permanent role actually owns that schema and can SET the target role. Verify effective database CREATE is false after revocation, including other membership/PUBLIC paths. Owner-scoped defaults apply only to future objects created with current_user equal to owner; an ordinary maintenance login merely inheriting owner rights does not inherit those defaults. Later fixed DDL must SET the owner or prove actual native migration ownership/ACL behavior. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-alterschema.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-alterdefaultprivileges.html .

A string checker for Dart must parse rather than grep: comments, `import` URIs and `${...}` interpolations all produce false positives, and machine identifiers such as `invalid-action-code` are matched against rather than displayed, so writing-guideline rule 17 puts them out of scope.

- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `flutter test` 300 passing and 7 skipped, up from 287 and 7 on `main`, with 13 new tests in `test/vocabulary_test.dart` and `test/widgets/caveat_text_test.dart` and no behavioural assertion weakened; `dart format` on every touched file; `python3 scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py` exits 0 with zero violations and an empty baseline, both with and without `--baseline`, where before this change 18 entries were baselined; `scripts/ci/verify.sh` fails only on `scripts/ci/test_release_sql_catalog.py::test_native_index_catalog_matches_ddl_and_rejects_valid_wrong_same_name`, a local PostgreSQL `pg_ctl` start that times out in this environment and touches no Dart.
- Durable learnings: A long lived feature branch can lose its base: `feat/theme-foundation` and `feat/writing-pass` both merged and were deleted during this task, so a prune, a merge of `origin/main` and a re-target to `main` was the recovery, and listing the remote heads is the cheap check before opening the pull request. The writing pass shipped its own `lib/src/widgets/caveat_text.dart` with a `why` parameter; the merge kept that file whole and this branch adapted its two call sites, which is cheaper than reconciling two spellings of one component. `riskComposite` changed its wording to "Not measured" and "62 of 100" in that same pass, so a test that pinned the old string failed on the merge, which is the reason to assert against the function rather than against a copied literal. `TextButton.icon` builds a private `TextButton` subclass, so `find.byType(TextButton)` and `find.widgetWithText(TextButton, ...)` never match it; tap the label text instead. `AnimatedSize` with a zero duration asserts "A RenderAnimatedSize was mutated in its own performLayout implementation", so a reduced-motion disclosure must drop the `AnimatedSize` entirely rather than pass it `Duration.zero`. A bare `Semantics(expanded:)` around a button does not merge into the button's node; wrap it in `MergeSemantics` so a screen reader reads one node. Intake used the visible status string as a state sentinel (`state.startsWith('Duplicate')` in three places), so renaming the chip needed a named constant, which is the pattern for any status string that logic also reads. Moving a caveat behind "Why" hides text that tests assert on; the honest test update is to assert the visible label and then tap "Why" and assert the body, which is a stronger assertion than the original. The string gate from `feat/ui-quality-gates` landed on `main` while this branch was in flight; rebasing before opening the pull request turned a hand-run grep into a real check and emptied the 18-entry ratchet in `scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt`. It caught the two bare `Yes` and `No` values in `reading_declarations.dart` that the hand grep did not, which became `_state(value, present, absent)` so each line names its own condition.
- Failed approaches: A first pass tried to keep `labelOf` at every call site and rename only whole strings, which left `needs_human_review` and `unmeasured` on screen; the fix was `lib/src/vocabulary.dart` with a whole-value map plus a per-word map for values the table does not name. Section 5 of the guidelines prescribes four caveat labels longer than the 40-character budget in rule 13 and section 7; the section 5 text was kept verbatim and the tension is recorded in the pull request rather than silently shortened.
- Remaining follow-ups: the baseline in `scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt` is now empty, so `--strict-baseline` can be turned on in CI. The confirmation-dialog surfaces that section 5 calls for are still inline text: `workspace.dart` conflict message stays a banner rather than a dialog, and the guideline's version number is not available on that error path. `capture_quality.dart` has no callback for a "Retake photograph" button. Checksums are shown in full rather than truncated to 12 characters with a copy action. The queue subtitle counts only loaded records. Those belong to steps 3 to 5 of the north star. Then step 3, shell and queue.

### 2026-09-14 - Shared component library (step 3 of the front-end north star)

- Task: Claude Code session, front-end design and development track, shared components
- Branch/worktree: `feat/shared-components` at `/Users/anuragduddu/code-projects/fieldmuseum/specimen-digitization-app/.claude/worktrees/agent-ab2a23bc7bab6fc6e`, branched from `feat/theme-foundation`, which was merged to `main` as PR #36 and deleted mid-task, so the pull request targets `main`
- Outcome: Completed; pull request open, not merged
- Commits/PRs: `6d647f6` (the component library and its tests) and `bdaa138` (merge of `origin/main`); PR <https://github.com/anurag-duddu/specimen-digitization-app/pull/38> against `main`
- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `flutter test` 396 passing and 7 skipped, and after merging `origin/main` 438 passing and 7 skipped, of which 142 are in `test/widgets/`; `dart format` on every touched file; `scripts/ci/verify.sh` ran the Flutter and Python suites, 2125 passed, 81 skipped, and one pre-existing environmental failure, `scripts/ci/test_release_sql_catalog.py::test_native_index_catalog_matches_ddl_and_rejects_valid_wrong_same_name`, which needs a local `pg_ctl` that this workstation does not have; that failure is unrelated to this branch. No existing screen file was changed, so the screens still render exactly as they did.
- Durable learnings: `TextButton.icon` builds a private `_TextButtonWithIcon` subclass, so `find.byType(TextButton)` finds nothing and `find.bySubtype<TextButton>()` is the durable form. `AnimatedSize` with a zero duration re-dirties itself inside its own `performLayout` and throws, so a reduced-motion path must drop the `AnimatedSize` entirely rather than pass it `Duration.zero`; the same will be true of any implicitly animated widget that measures its child. `Semantics(label:)` as a parent of an `InkWell` produces two nodes, not one, so a row that wants to read as a single phrase needs `MergeSemantics` around the pair plus `ExcludeSemantics` around the row's own text. Setting `excludeSemantics: true` on a `Semantics` that wraps an `InkWell` silently removes the tap action, which is the accessible failure mode to avoid. `matchesSemantics` is a whole-node matcher and is brittle for one flag; `containsSemantics` is the partial one. `@Preview` only accepts literals and public symbols, so a shared theme helper for previews has to be public. Every action row that carries a verb phrase needs `Wrap`, not `Row`: "Supersede the decision" plus "Cancel" overflows a 480 dialog at the default text scale.
- Failed approaches: A first pass gave `StatusChip` a closure-valued field so one constructor could resolve either a status or a prepared presentation; that cannot be `const`, so it was replaced by two nullable fields and two const constructors. A `Colors.transparent` leading bar was used to hold the queue row's layout stable between selected and unselected; it is a literal the design system's own grep gate forbids, so the border is now conditional and the padding makes up the width instead. `RiskMeter` could not be made a `const` constructor because its assert calls a static method, so its tests construct it without `const`.
- Remaining follow-ups: Adopt these components in the screens, which is where the eight remaining color literals in `workspace.dart` and `workbench.dart` disappear. Field states have no glyphs in `theme/icons.dart` yet, so `SpecimenStatus` names its own for the seven field values; fold them into `SpecimenIconography` when the theme file is next touched. `EvidenceDrawer` is an inline disclosure rather than the side sheet the design system describes for windows at 900 and above; the side sheet arrives with the responsive step. `ReasonSheet` does not yet render the diff of what will change, because it has no record to diff against until the screens adopt it.

A `SelectableText` exposes a long-press action, which makes a 20 dp line a tap target the android and iOS guidelines correctly refuse; the record identifier became plain text plus a 48 dp copy control. `Shortcuts` only fires while focus is inside its subtree, so a keyboard map needs a `FocusScope(autofocus: true)` under the `Actions` or no key ever reaches it, and a widget test that sends keys will silently do nothing. `AnimatedRotation` does not re-lay-out, so a non-square photograph overflows mid-turn; `RotatedBox` swaps the constraints and keeps the image inside the pane, at the cost of the animated quarter turn the motion catalog asks for. A fixed-height pinned header plus a decision bar overflows a short window; a loose `Flexible` around a `SizedBox` at the blueprint's fraction gives the fraction when the window can afford it and takes the difference out of the photograph when it cannot.

- Durable learnings: The manifest is the honest surface. Splitting `ManifestEntry.state` into an `UploadState` enum plus a separate one-sentence `reason` (H4.5) is what makes the other five intake findings cheap: a rejected file becomes a Skipped row with its own reason instead of a banner (H1.6, H9.4), the header can count states (H1.5), and Stop can name what it cancelled (H3.7). Keep a `displayState` getter that returns Checking while a round trip is in flight rather than overwriting `state`, so the row returns to the state it actually had. Progress belongs to the entry, not to the callback: `observeProgress` clamps to a monotonic maximum so a resumed upload reporting a lower server offset never runs the ring backwards. Every screen that uses `lib/src/widgets/` must be pumped under `AppTheme.light()`; a bare `MaterialApp` has no theme extensions and every shared component throws a null check on `context.space`. `tester.binding.setSurfaceSize` does not move `MediaQuery.sizeOf`, so a test of a width branch must set `tester.view.physicalSize` and `devicePixelRatio` instead. A lazy `ListView` does not build rows below the fold, so a layout test at a short height finds nothing; give it the height or assert on the widget's own configuration. `addTearDown` runs after the framework's own end-of-test checks for `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride` and for an open `SemanticsHandle`, so both must be restored or disposed inline in the test body. Two identical fixture files hash to one checksum and therefore collapse into one manifest row, which is correct behaviour and a trap for any test that wants N rows. A `Semantics(label:)` placed outside a `GestureDetector` leaves the detector's own unlabelled tap node in the tree and fails `labeledTapTargetGuideline`; put the `Semantics` outside with `excludeSemantics: true` and move anything that needs its own announcement, such as the focus lock indicator, out of that subtree.
- Failed approaches: A first Stop test drove the batch inside `tester.runAsync` with a `Completer` and polling; tapping inside `runAsync` hung the test. The correction was to give the fake repository no timers at all, so the whole batch runs on microtasks and plain `tester.pump()` moves it along, with one extra pump after the state changes so the frame that draws it is rendered. `find.bySemanticsLabel` did not match a label declared on a nested `Semantics` widget; `tester.getSemantics` on a keyed node plus an assertion on the visible glyph is the durable form.

### 2026-09-14 — Front-end north star step 6: motion and polish

- Task: `feat/motion-and-polish`
- Branch/worktree: `feat/motion-and-polish` at `/Users/anuragduddu/code-projects/fieldmuseum/specimen-digitization-app/.claude/worktrees/agent-a44bb40017c82ba1e`
- Outcome: In progress
- Commits/PRs: see the pull request opened from this branch against `main`
- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `flutter test` 624 passing,
  7 skipped (all seven are live-API suites gated on environment variables);
  `flutter test test/accessibility/` green; `dart format` on every touched file;
  `python3 scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py --baseline scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt`
  reports zero violations; `test/theme/no_color_literals_test.dart` reports zero
  literals outside `lib/src/theme/`.
- Durable learnings:
  - **A nested `Navigator` erases the semantics of everything painted before it
    in the same semantics boundary.** A route's modal barrier sets
    `isBlockingSemanticsOfPreviouslyPaintedNodes`, and an app shell that paints
    its chrome before the routed child therefore disappears from the
    accessibility tree entirely: the navigation rail and the environment band
    produced no nodes at all while looking perfectly normal on screen. The fix
    is one line, `Semantics(container: true, explicitChildNodes: true)` around
    the routed child, which keeps the blocking inside the route. Any shell that
    wraps a `Navigator` needs it, and only a semantics-tree assertion catches
    it: the four `flutter_test` guideline matchers all pass on a screen whose
    chrome is invisible, because they only inspect the nodes that exist.
  - **`Flexible(fit: loose)` strands the space it does not use.** Where one
    child has a target height and another needs a floor, the flex algorithm
    cannot express it: a loose child is capped at its share and the remainder
    stays in its slot rather than passing to the `Expanded`. The workable shape
    is to measure the fixed chrome with a `RenderProxyBox` that reports its
    height on the next frame, then size the flexible part arithmetically. The
    photograph pinned above the workbench evidence needed exactly this, and the
    symptom of getting it wrong was a scroll view with a zero-height viewport,
    which on a device reads as "the screen is frozen" rather than as a layout
    bug.
  - **A sticky bar inside the scrolling pane's own flex share eats that share.**
    The decision bar was a sibling of the evidence scroll view inside the pane,
    so the pane's 50 percent of the column went to the bar first. Lifting the
    bar out to the enclosing column is what made the pane scrollable again.
  - **`tester.hasRunningAnimations` is not usable after `tester.tap`.** Material's
    ink splash is a running animation and reduced motion does not stop it; the
    policy drops ripples through the theme. Reduced-motion tests drive state by
    rebuilding with a new value rather than by pressing a control, and where a
    press is unavoidable they assert on the tree and on the value instead.
  - **`find.bySemanticsLabel` misses merged labels.** A label folded into an
    ancestor node belongs to no widget, so the finder returns nothing while a
    screen reader reads it perfectly well. Walk the tree from
    `tester.getSemantics(find.byType(MaterialApp))` and collect both `label`
    and `tooltip`: an icon-only control names itself through its tooltip.
  - **`MediaQuery` carries no reduced-motion signal on iOS and none at all on
    web in Flutter 3.38.5.** The client reads four sources: `MediaQuery`'s
    `disableAnimations` for Android, `AccessibilityFeatures.reduceMotion` for
    iOS, a hand-written `matchMedia` bridge for web, and a stored in-app
    preference. `AccessibilityFeatures` is not inherited, so a `MotionScope`
    above the router rebuilds on `didChangeAccessibilityFeatures`.
  - **`NavigationRail` with `labelType: none` contributes no semantics for its
    destinations**, because the label widget is simply not built. A collapsed
    rail is a column of unnamed buttons unless the words are drawn or a label is
    supplied by hand.
  - **`Image.memory` without `gaplessPlayback` blanks on every rebuild that
    resolves a new provider instance**, which is what made the specimen
    photograph flash black on a panel change.
- Failed approaches:
  - Trying to reproduce the phone scrolling defect at 390x844 with a plain
    scaffold host, and then through the real router, both passed. The condition
    that reproduces it is a short viewport plus a system inset, where the
    wrapped decision bar consumes the pane's whole share. A regression test that
    cannot fail is worse than none; the squeezed-viewport case is the one that
    holds this.
  - Computing the pinned photograph's height from `MediaQuery.sizeOf`. That is
    the window, not the pane, and on a phone the two differ by the app bar, the
    navigation bar, the environment band, the progress row and the insets.
  - Giving the photograph a larger flex so it could exceed half the remainder.
    It cannot: see the stranded-space note above.

- Task: `verify/frontend-overhaul`

- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean, "No issues found". `flutter test` 739 passing and 10 skipped, up from 624 and 7 on the base branch; the three new skips each name a finding in `design/08-verification-report.md`. `python3 scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py --baseline scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt` reports 95 files scanned and 0 violations. `test/theme/no_color_literals_test.dart` reports 0 literals outside `lib/src/theme/` with an empty backlog. `flutter build web --release` succeeds. `bash scripts/ci/build_mobile.sh android` succeeds using the JDK bundled with Android Studio; note that the script refuses to run while `lib/firebase_options.dart` exists, so a local copy of `firebase_options.ci.dart` has to be removed first and restored afterwards. 97 goldens generated and every one inspected; the findings are in the report.
- Durable learnings: A `Semantics(hint:)` wrapped around a disabled button leaves the hint on a parent node, so a screen reader focusing the control hears its name and "dimmed" and never the reason; `MergeSemantics` is what folds it onto the control's own node, and four controls in this client were silent that way. A merge boundary keeps its own flags rather than the merged data's, so a merged node must repeat `enabled:` itself, otherwise both screen readers and `textContrastGuideline` treat a disabled control as live; that is how a correct accessibility fix turned four contrast tests red until the flag was added. Walking a semantics tree with `node.visitChildren` descends into merged subtrees and prints controls the platform never receives, which makes one control look like two findings; stop at `node.mergeAllDescendantsIntoThisNode`. `SemanticsFlags` in Flutter 3.38.5 is tristate: `isSelected` and `isEnabled` are `Tristate` and `isChecked` is `CheckedState`, and the `hasXState` getters are gone. `LoadingAnnouncement`-style live regions whose invisible branch is `SizedBox.shrink()` produce a node with an empty rect, and an empty rect is dropped from the tree, so the announcement that exists to break a silent wait is itself silent. `flutter test` folds a second and later exception into one "multiple exceptions were detected" summary that no longer names any of them, so a test that wants to classify layout errors has to install its own `FlutterError.onError` rather than draining `takeException`. Goldens rendered in the deterministic test font show text as boxes, which is exactly right for a CI gate and still shows overflow, clipping, an empty pane, a missing element and the wrong theme; pair them with device screenshots for copy. A golden that merely renders proves nothing about the control it is supposed to show: the region-editor goldens captured the record screen with a correctly disabled edit control until the test asserted the editor was actually on screen.
- Failed approaches: Fixing the app-bar collection switcher's clipped floating label with vertical padding alone. A 48 dp outlined field draws its label across its own top border, so the label needs about 5.5 dp above the field and the toolbar's 56 dp leaves only 4; padding moved the overhang from 5.5 dp to 1.5 dp and no further without dropping the field below the 48 dp target. The real fix is to stop using a form field as an app-bar action. Asserting a region overlay and its chip share a name against the default record fixture, which carries an unverified original: the workbench correctly refuses to draw overlays on one of those, so the assertion tested nothing until a second fixture with a known display transform was added. Scoping a segment tap with a bare `find.text`, which at 200 percent text hit a different control and captured a dialog over the record in eight goldens.
- Remaining follow-ups: The fourteen findings in `apps/specimen_digitization/design/08-verification-report.md`, ranked, each with its exact fix. The three severity-1 items are the record screen overflowing and dropping the photograph on a phone and at 200 percent text at every width (V-1), `J` and `K` bound and documented but wired to a callback the record screen never supplies (V-2), and a deep link to a record cancelling the in-flight queue load so the list pane claims the collection is empty (V-5). VoiceOver and TalkBack were not run on hardware in this verification, so accessibility section 4.2 steps 1 to 7 remain manual and unperformed for this release cycle. ### 2026-09-14 - Front-end step 7 follow-up: closing the verification defects

- Task: `fix/verification-defects`
- Branch/worktree: `fix/verification-defects` at `/Users/anuragduddu/code-projects/fieldmuseum/specimen-digitization-app/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6c40af121c6952fe`, branched from `origin/verify/frontend-overhaul`
- Outcome: Completed; pull request open against `main`, not merged. It contains all of PR #44, which it supersedes.
- Commits/PRs: see the pull request opened from this branch against `main`
- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean, "No issues found". `flutter test` 768 passing and 7 skipped, up from 739 and 10: the three skips that recorded findings V-2, V-3 and V-4 are gone, because each is now an assertion that runs. `python3 scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py --baseline scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt` reports 97 files scanned and 0 violations. `test/theme/no_color_literals_test.dart` reports 0 literals outside `lib/src/theme/` with an empty backlog. `flutter build web --release` succeeds. All 97 goldens regenerated and the affected ones inspected with an image reader; `knownWorkbenchOverflows` is empty and the suite fails on an overflow anywhere.
- Durable learnings:
  - **A fixed-height box around a pane whose own chrome is unmeasured is the bug, not the number inside it.** V-1 was `pinnedSourceMinHeight = 160` where the pane's controls and region chips needed about 250. Raising the number would have moved the failure rather than removed it. The fix that holds is to hand the pane a band for its pixels and let the pane be exactly as tall as its parts, then measure the whole pane and subtract the band to learn the chrome. That measurement is non-circular, and the pane can never be handed a box shorter than its own rows.
  - **Measure with `MeasuredHeight` into a parts map, and make the first frame use the form that cannot overflow.** A layout that needs a measurement has one frame without it. Goldens collect layout errors from every frame, so a transient overflow fails the suite exactly like a permanent one. The scrolling form is the safe first frame; the pinned form starts once the numbers are in, and the plan is a pure function of the measurements so it cannot oscillate.
  - **At 200 percent text a phone hands the record screen about 200 logical pixels.** The app bar, the environment banner, the navigation bar, the back control and the insets take the rest. The decision bar alone is taller than that, so "pin the bar" has to be a decision the layout makes rather than a structure it assumes.
  - **Pin the photograph, not the record header.** On a stacked layout the record's title and identifier now scroll with the evidence. That is what buys the pinned photograph enough height to exist on a phone, and it is the right trade: the pixels are what every correction is checked against.
  - **One generation counter cannot guard two independent loads.** V-5 was `refresh` and `openSpecimen` sharing `_generation`. Splitting them is the fix; the second half is that a list which has never been answered must render placeholders rather than an empty state, because "no records" and "not asked yet" are different claims and only one of them is the collection's.
  - **A test that installs `FlutterError.onError` must restore it before its own `expect`.** Otherwise the failure is swallowed by the collector and the binding reports "a test overrode FlutterError.onError" with no sign of what actually failed. This cost an hour.
  - **Drive a golden's state from the keyboard rather than a tap where the layout can scroll.** A tap needs a hit test, a hit test needs a position, and a position that depends on a scroll offset makes the capture a capture of a scrolled pane. The segment shortcuts move the selection and move nothing else.
  - **Goldens are host-specific in their bytes and host-independent in their evidence.** Linux antialiases the deterministic test font differently from macOS and moves 1 to 4 percent of the pixels in half the files. The image comparison is now skipped off macOS with the reason printed; every layout and semantics assertion, including the overflow check that carries V-1, still runs everywhere.
  - **A `TextEditingController` created inside a `showDialog` builder and disposed in `whenComplete` is disposed while the route is still animating out.** The dialog has to be a `StatefulWidget` that owns it.
  - **`SemanticsRole.tabBar` and `SemanticsRole.tab` in `dart:ui` turn a `SegmentedButton` into something VoiceOver reads as a tab list** without replacing it with a `TabBar`, which would have moved every workbench golden and the segment intents.
  - **`MediaQuery.supportsAnnounceOf` gates `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement`, and it is false by default in a widget test.** A test for an announcement has to set `supportsAnnounce: true` on a `MediaQuery` and capture `SystemChannels.accessibility` with `setMockDecodedMessageHandler`.
- Failed approaches:
  - Collapsing the source pane's view controls into an overflow menu below a fixed width threshold of 360. Five 48 dp targets fit comfortably at 390, so the threshold fired on every phone and moved four controls one tap further away for no reason, and it broke a geometry test that taps Rotate. The threshold is now the width the row actually needs, computed from the number of controls.
  - Changing `Flexible` to `Expanded` in the filter form to stop the risk switch being painted over Apply. The form is pumped into an unbounded height by four accessibility tests, and `Expanded` there is an assertion failure. The defect was never the flex fit: it was `showAdaptiveForm` putting the form in a dialog with no height bound, so "the remaining space" was infinite and the scrolling body shrink-wrapped its whole content.
  - Reading the stacked layout's available height and assuming the record header belonged in the fixed chrome. Counting it there is what kept the phone in the scrolling form at normal text: with the header out of the arithmetic and inside the evidence scroll, the same window pins the photograph.
- Remaining follow-ups:
  - Four criteria stay Partial for reasons outside the client: 7.2 (the wire takes one decision per call, so five corrections are five calls), 7.3 (no bulk action exists on the API), 10.3 (no collection document this client has seen publishes an administrator contact, and the sign-in messages are raised before a collection is resolved), 10.4 (not verifiable from a repository).
  - Three stay Partial and are client work someone should schedule: 1.2 (no test measures the 200 ms and the one second), 7.6 (configured reason codes are not read from the profile), 10.2 (a term in a row is not itself a link to its definition).
  - Findings V-7, V-8, V-9 and the new V-15 are open, each with its exact fix in `design/08-verification-report.md`. V-8 in particular is a single theme change that moves most of the 97 goldens, so it wants its own pull request.
  - VoiceOver and TalkBack have still not been run on hardware. The device screenshots under `design/screenshots/rebuild/` predate PR #43 and all of this, and should be retaken.

- Task: front-end verification closeout, third pass
- Branch/worktree: `fix/verification-remainder` at `/Users/anuragduddu/code-projects/fieldmuseum/specimen-digitization-app/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae378c972c37f4262`

- Validation: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` no issues; `flutter test` 846 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed; `python3 scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py --baseline scripts/ci/ui_strings_baseline.txt` 100 files, 0 violations; `test/theme/no_color_literals_test.dart` 0 literals with an empty backlog; `flutter build web --release` built `build/web`. Goldens and semantics fixtures regenerated on macOS with `--update-goldens` and a sample of the regenerated PNGs read back. `scripts/ci/verify.sh` was not run: it also runs the whole Python suite, which this change does not touch.
- Durable learnings:
  - A design token that exists is not a token that ships. `disabled.content` had been in `SpecimenColors` and in the design system since the token pass, and `test/theme/contrast_test.dart` had been asserting it, while every disabled control in the product drew at Material's 38 percent default because no component theme was given the token. A contrast test over the token table proves the table, not the screen. The component themes now take `SpecimenColors` and pass the pair on, which is where the check should have been all along.
  - `MinimumTapTargetGuideline` skips nodes flagged `isLink` (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 exempts inline links). That is what makes an inline definition affordance possible at all: a domain word inside a sentence cannot be given a 48 dp box without breaking the sentence. `Semantics(link: true, onTap: ...)` passes the tap-target and labelled-target guidelines; `Semantics(button: true)` would have failed the first.
  - A semantics node that carries an action of its own is not merged into its parent. Turning three labels inside `FieldRow` into definition links silently emptied the row's spoken summary, which had been relying on the merge. Any component whose label comes from merged descendants is one child action away from losing it; state the label explicitly instead.
  - Timing criteria need a gated fake, not a delay and not `pumpAndSettle`. Hold the repository on a `Completer`, `tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 200))` to advance the test clock by exactly the budget, assert, complete the gate, `pump(const Duration(seconds: 1))`, assert the result. A settle waits however long the control takes, which is the thing being measured.
  - Watching a save land frame by frame found a defect three passes of review had not: `_savingLocally` was cleared when the save's future completed, but the host notifies during that await and the rebuild lands a frame later, so `didUpdateWidget` saw the new revision with the flag already false and raised "another reviewer saved" on the reviewer's own decision. Clear such a flag in a post-frame callback. No `pumpAndSettle` test could see it, because the banner went up and back down inside one call.
  - A golden can be checked in stale. Two workbench goldens had been committed with an empty source pane, captured before the photograph decoded, and were failing on `main` before this branch touched anything. Read the failure images rather than regenerating on reflex; here the new image was the correct one.
  - Grep the wire fixtures before designing around a key. `reason_codes` exists, but it is the machine's reasons a record is in the queue, not a reviewer's decision vocabulary. Reading one as the other would have been a quiet mislabelling; they now sit under separate headings and `configuredReasonKeys` deliberately excludes the name.
- Failed approaches:
  - Setting `ChipThemeData.labelStyle` and `InputDecorationTheme.labelStyle` to a `WidgetStateTextStyle` in order to colour the disabled label. Both replace the component's default style wholesale rather than layering on it, so the selected chip lost its `onSecondaryContainer` label and failed the contrast guideline. The safer correction is `disabledForegroundColor` on the button styles, which is state-scoped, plus `disabledBorder` on the input, and leaving the chip label alone.
  - Capping the app bar switcher with a `ConstrainedBox` inside the `TextButton`. The button's own padding sits outside it, so the control measured 283.7 against a 280 cap. The constraint belongs outside the button.
  - Making `_rememberReason` await the preferences store before sending the save. `SharedPreferences.getInstance()` never completes in a widget test with no mock values, so the save never went out. A convenience must not gate a decision: update in memory, persist behind the save, and swallow a store that will not open.
- Remaining follow-ups: pass criteria 7.2, 7.3, 10.3 and 10.4 stay Partial. 7.2 needs `POST .../decisions:batch`; 7.3 needs an action across records; 10.3 needs either a collection document that publishes a contact or `--dart-define=SPECIMEN_ADMIN_CONTACT` in the deployment; 10.4 needs two people who have not seen the app. The device screenshots in `design/screenshots/` still predate pull request #43 and should be retaken, and no device capture exists of an account with more than one collection, so the new switcher is unverified on hardware.

  - A batch call silently drops a guarantee the one at a time path gets for free. #42's loop re-checks between sends that a draft is still current, because a readback has reached the widget by then; a batch cannot re-read the screen between its own calls. The composition is to hand the check down: `reviewBatch` takes a `stillApplies` predicate and asks it against the record each call produced, and refuses a result that is not a newer version of the same record.
  - An idempotency key and a batch prefix are two different jobs. Naming every call `<prefix>-<index>` looks tidy and breaks retry reconciliation, because a retry of the remaining corrections mints a new prefix and therefore a new key for a call whose answer was uncertain. The prefix names the batch for whoever reads the server's log; the key identifies the decision and has to be memoised on the record version it was sent against, exactly as `WorkspaceController.mutate` already did for a single decision. #42's `product_acceptance_regressions_test.dart` caught this, which is what a regression test is for.
  - Resolving a binary golden conflict by taking either side is only safe if regenerating the whole suite afterwards changes nothing. Here it changed no byte, which is the evidence that the two branches' renders agree; without that check "take either side" is a guess.
- Failed approaches: naming batch calls positionally off the prefix alone, which passed every test on this branch and failed #42's retry-key regression the moment the two met. The safer correction is above.
- Remaining follow-ups: unchanged from the previous entry. Pass criteria 7.2, 7.3, 10.3 and 10.4 stay Partial, and the batch endpoint 7.2 proposes would also be safer than what ships, because one `expected_revision` for the whole set puts the still-applies decision on the server rather than the client.

A new merge commit can never match a packet frozen earlier, so the plane fails closed on source mismatch. The `data-*`/`runtime-*` environments carry only `branch_policy`, no required reviewers, so this interlock is the only thing standing between a merge and a privileged job.

Account-change invalidation must bump **both**, or an in-flight queue load from the previous account can land in the new session. A blind rename during conflict resolution would have introduced exactly that.

### 2026-09-14 — Workstream E: multi-select in the queue and a bulk decisions endpoint

- Task: Claude Code session, workstream E of `docs/execution/SOURCE_BROWSE_AND_RUN.md` (design PR [#56](https://github.com/anurag-duddu/specimen-digitization-app/pull/56))
- Branch/worktree: `claude/nostalgic-rubin-f4bc3a` at `.claude/worktrees/nostalgic-rubin-f4bc3a`
- Outcome: Completed. Pass criterion 7.3 and defect V-13 are closed; 7.2 keeps its Partial verdict and changes its reason. Nothing was deployed.
- Commits/PRs: [PR #59](https://github.com/anurag-duddu/specimen-digitization-app/pull/59), commits `95421c4` (feature), `68494c8` (contract, report, blueprint, closeout), `38e9fcc` and `999e6e7` (two shared-widget fixes found by the workstream D session building on this branch).
- Validation: `uv run pytest -q` 2,460 passed / 81 skipped; `flutter test` 922 passed / 7 skipped; `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `scripts/ci/check_ui_strings.py` 0 violations, 0 baselined; `uvx pre-commit run` on the staged set passed. Goldens regenerated on macOS: 26 moved, 8 added, 97 files to 105.

- Durable learnings:
  - **`GET /specimens` blanks `available_actions` on every row on purpose** (`api.py`, "Metadata rows lack pilot pins and lease state"). The queue therefore cannot know in advance which records will accept a decision. That is not an inconvenience to work around, it is the argument for the endpoint's shape: per-record outcomes are the only honest way to report a bulk action from a list that cannot pre-filter. Anything that wants to grey out a bulk control per row has to fetch detail first, which defeats the point.
  - **The list rows do carry `revision` and `record_version_id`** (`search.py:247`), so a bulk call can send the same optimistic concurrency token the single route demands. But the workspace response is renamed to `latest_record_version_id` on the way into the client (`api_repository.dart:909`), so a `Specimen` built from the list and one built from the workbench spell it differently. `Specimen.recordVersionId` now reads both; anything new that needs the token should use it rather than a literal key.
  - **A batch endpoint that reuses the single-decision handler must special-case `WorkspaceTooLarge`.** `decision()` commits and then renders, and an oversized render raises after the write with `mutation_committed: true`. Catching it as a refusal would tell the reviewer the opposite of what happened to the record. It is caught separately and reported as applied, threading the revision out of `exc.details`.
  - **Error classification had to come out of the exception handler** into `classify_error`. A batch row must name the same code the same decision would have been given on its own route, and a second copy of that mapping would drift silently: the reviewer would be told a different thing depending on how the decision was sent.
  - **Decisions on one record must be threaded server side, not client side.** Each save moves the revision, so a client sending two decisions for one record at one `expected_revision` would have the second refused as a conflict. The client names the base once and the server applies each against what the one before it produced. The verification report predicted this is strictly safer, and it is: the server decides whether a later correction still applies.
  - **"Select all" over a cursor-paged list has to be decided, not defaulted.** It means every record loaded, and that is now structural rather than documented: `PagedSelection` has no way to express "all matching". The list API answers a page and a cursor and never a total, and the endpoint takes named records at named versions, so the other reading would claim authority over records the client has never seen and could not state a count on a confirmation that exists to state one. A different list can legitimately reach further, and workstream D's source inventory is one: it is an immutable snapshot with a server-stated count and generation-pinned rows. That belongs in a second type alongside `PagedSelection`, not a mode inside it, because the model's whole value is `count == items.length`.
  - **A selection must be pruned to what is loaded on every sync**, or the count includes records the reviewer can no longer see. A live selection also takes `holdList()`, the same hold a focused row and an open sheet already take: the count on a confirmation must not move between being read and being confirmed.
  - **Reconcile a selection from the controller's listener, not from `build`.** Releasing a list hold can apply a deferred page and notify, and doing that during a build throws.
  - **A bare `GestureDetector(onLongPress:)` fails `labeledTapTargetGuideline`**: it puts an action on an unnamed node, so a screen reader is told an action exists and not what it is. Declare it as `Semantics(label:, onLongPress:, onLongPressHint:)` around a detector with `excludeFromSemantics: true`. Caught by `test/widget_test.dart`, "narrow layout and large text", not by any test written for the feature.
  - **A `Wrap` inside a `Row` reports its unwrapped intrinsic width**, so the `Row` sizes it for one long line and it overflows at every width below that. The fix was deleting the breakpoint, not raising it: the count and the controls are one `Wrap`, correct at 360 dp, at 1440 dp and at 200 percent text with no tuned number.
  - **`find.byType(FilledButton)` does not match `FilledButton.icon`**, which builds a private subclass. Match by role with `find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w is FilledButton)` or `ButtonStyleButton`.
  - **A top-level helper exported through `widgets.dart` lands in every screen's namespace.** A function named `records(int)` shadowed a local in an unrelated test and broke compilation; it is `recordsLabel` now. Barrel exports need names that read as owned.
  - **Which goldens move is itself evidence.** The four compact queue goldens did not move, and that is the proof that a narrow window has no checkbox column until a long press opens one. The 12 workbench goldens that moved are all at `large`, where the queue list sits beside the record. Checking the set that moved against the set expected caught nothing wrong this time, which is the point of checking.

- Failed approaches:
  - Reading a regenerated golden PNG by eye and concluding the compact dark bar rendered with light-theme colours. It did not: sampling the pixels gave `#262B27` and the dark-mode primary. Sample the pixels before reporting a colour bug in a golden.
  - Every intake call in a backend test sharing one `Idempotency-Key`. The server reconciles on the key, so the second batch with a different payload is a 409 "Idempotency payload mismatch", not a second record. Per-call keys.
  - Identical image bytes for several specimens in a test: checksum deduplication is real (`specimen_scope_checksum`), so they collapse into one record. Vary the pixels.

- Remaining follow-ups:
  - **7.2 is one client change from Pass.** `WorkspaceController.mutateBatch` still reaches `reviewBatch`, the fan-out extension, rather than `SpecimenRepository.reviewMany`, which this session added to the interface and implemented as one call. Moving it needs no change to `workbench.dart`'s own call site, but it rewrites nine tests in `test/review_batch_test.dart` and the save path in files a concurrent session owned, so it was deliberately left. `stillApplies` has no meaning in a single call; the server's one `expected_revision` replaces it.
  - The bulk bar offers approve and confirm coverage only. Defer, which the blueprint names, is a run action on `/runs/{run_id}/actions` rather than a decision, so it needs its own batch route or its own design; assign has no model at all.
  - Workstream D asked for a "select all matching" mode on `PagedSelection` for its snapshot listing, and the wire settled it against the mode: `POST /batches/{batch_id}/items:from-source` takes `objects: [{object_name, generation}]`, at most 50, and the generation is the integrity story on that path, so an object that has not been listed cannot be named. A whole-snapshot selection has nothing to send. "Select all 1,000" therefore means "page the rest of the snapshot in, then select it", which is safe because the snapshot is immutable and a cursor is bound to it, and which leaves `count == items.length` untouched. The invariant was load-bearing in a way neither session had evidence for beforehand. Both sessions would have built the wrong thing from the design doc alone.
  - **A shared row widget must separate "this list is selecting" from "this row can be selected".** `SelectableRow.showCheckbox` started out doing both, and hiding the control on a per-row basis takes the leading column with it, so one unselectable row makes every row below it read against a different left edge. It only bites a list where selectability varies per row, which the queue is not and a source inventory is: a photograph whose media type the source does not admit cannot be imported. `enabled: false` now draws the control disabled instead. Hidden and disabled also read differently to a screen reader: absent, it says nothing and the reviewer cannot tell an unselectable row from one they missed. The regression test asserts the content's left edge is identical either way.
  - What that exchange did change is the shared widgets: the header claimed none of the three pieces mentions a specimen, and three strings quietly did. `SelectionBar` now takes `countLabel` and `moreMatchLabel` and `SelectableRow` takes `longPressHint`, all defaulting to the record wording, so a list of storage objects that nothing has imported says "6 objects selected" rather than calling them records, which is the distinction that screen exists to draw. The lesson is not the three strings: a component that claims to be list-agnostic has to have that claim checked against a second list, because every hardcoded noun in it reads correct until there is one.
  - **Another session's merge of this branch hit a real conflict in the exception handler.** This session lifted the classification into `classify_error`; the source-registry branch added a stale-generation mapping inline. Git kept the function and folded in `SnapshotTooLarge` but silently dropped `SourceObjectChanged`, because its `from .source_reader import` had nothing to anchor to, and either side taken whole reports a stale-generation import as 503 `runtime_unavailable` instead of 422 `source_object_changed`. Resolved on their branch by keeping both. Anyone merging both branches should check that line rather than trust the automatic resolution.
  - No cloud provisioning, deployment, IAM change or paid inference was performed by this session.

## 2026-09-14 — Workstream D: browse a registered source and add photographs to the queue

- Task: workstream D of `docs/execution/SOURCE_BROWSE_AND_RUN.md`. Branch `claude/source-browse-screen`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/interesting-mirzakhani-e0cadf`, stacked on `claude/eager-chatelet-20b3af` (workstreams A and B) and `claude/nostalgic-rubin-f4bc3a` (the shared selection model), both merged in rather than forked. [PR #61](https://github.com/anurag-duddu/specimen-digitization-app/pull/61); commits `e50e67e` (model and repository), `bd08414` (the screen), `af25f1c` (the disabled row), `badfddf` (two writing rules), `1ecd81d` (narrow-window tests), plus merges of both sibling branches and `origin/main`.
- Outcome: the screen ships. `scripts/ci/verify.sh` passed on the settled merged tree (2,591 backend passed / 81 skipped, full Flutter suite, `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean, `check_ui_strings.py` 0 violations and 0 baselined, web release build, terminal "All local CI gates passed"). All nine required GitHub checks pass on PR #61; Hosting deploy skips, as it must on a pull request. A reviewer opens Intake, follows "Add from storage" into a registered source, filters by All / Not in queue / In queue, picks one, several or all, and adds the selection to the queue behind a confirmation that names the count. No cloud provisioning, deployment, IAM change or paid inference was performed by this session.

- Durable learnings:
  - **The wire, not taste, decided what "select all" can mean.** `POST /batches/{batch_id}/items:from-source` takes `objects: [{object_name, generation}]`, at most 50, and the generation is the whole integrity story on that path: it replaces the client declaration that upload completion checks against. A generation exists only on a listing row, so a photograph the client has not loaded is one it could not send. "Select all 1,000" therefore means "page the rest of the snapshot in, then select it". Both this session and the selection model's author had independently assumed a filter-expanding import (`{source_id, entries_sha256, filter}`), which is the shape the design doc reads like and is not what landed. Reading the endpoint settled a design argument that neither transcript could have.
  - **`matching_count` is exact or absent, never estimated, and absent is not zero.** `media_type` is on the inventory row so filtering by it is a free in-memory scan; `imported` resolves through `find_checksum`, one round trip per object, so counting a snapshot under that filter would cost a lookup per object on every page. The server returns `null` instead of guessing. The client carries the null through to the screen, where the select-all control is **absent rather than vague**, because a control that cannot name its reach cannot be confirmed against. Rendering `null` as "0" would have been the exact failure writing rule 14 exists to prevent.
  - **A confirmation must not name a number no endpoint reports.** The brief asked the confirmation to name the count, the estimated cost and the remaining allowance. The count is real. The other two are not: workstream C is explicitly blocked on an ongoing budget the owner has not set, `CollectionProfile.cost_micros` is server-side only, and no allowance concept is exposed to the client at all. Importing also dispatches nothing, in any mode. So the confirmation says "No model runs and no allowance is used." — which is what it costs — and the screen carries **no run control**, because an affordance the server cannot serve is hidden rather than disabled (blueprint 3) and the north star's rule for data the API does not return is an honest absence rather than a placeholder. The confirmation component takes the count today and is where the estimate and allowance attach when C lands.
  - **Thumbnails are placeholders by decision.** An un-imported object has no asset, so `GET /assets/{id}/content` does not address it, and the originals are ~300 KB each. A row that *is* already a record carries `specimen_id` and not `asset_id`, so reaching its real image would be a `/specimens/{id}` fetch per row across a grid. Both paths are refused; `SpecimenThumbnail` already draws the placeholder the intake list uses. A source thumbnail endpoint keyed by `(source_id, object_name, generation)` is the upgrade, and the generation in that key is what stops a cached render outliving the bytes it depicts.
  - **"Object" is storage's word and did not belong on screen.** The vocabulary table has no row for it, the reviewer is looking at photographs of specimens, every media type a source admits is an image, and `lib/` already says "photograph" 139 times. The screen counts photographs. "Source" did need a glossary row and got one in the same commit, which is what rule 7 asks for.
  - **A separate repository interface keeps a screen's dependencies honest.** `SourceRepository` sits beside `SpecimenRepository` rather than extending it, so the screen takes the three calls it uses and a fake in a test implements three methods instead of the whole client API. It also meant adding the surface broke no existing fake. `sourcesIn(repository)` is the one place that asks whether a build serves sources; where it answers null the control is hidden, which is why the intake goldens did not move when the entry point was added.
  - **Reached from Intake rather than as a third navigation destination.** Adding from a source creates a batch through the same batch-and-items surface an upload does, so it is the same errand by another route in. A third destination would also have churned every shell, queue, workbench and intake golden while two other sessions were regenerating goldens, which is a merge hazard this repository has already been bitten by.
  - **Which goldens moved was the check, twice.** Adding the screen: 8 added, 0 modified, so nothing overlapped the other sessions' regenerations. Taking `SelectableRow.enabled`: exactly 6 moved, all at medium and above, and the two compact goldens did not, which is the proof that the checkbox column is closed on a narrow window. The set that moves is evidence about the change, not a rubber stamp.
  - **A golden caught a defect no test asserted.** Hiding the checkbox on unselectable rows let them slide left by the column width, breaking the alignment a reviewer scans a thousand rows down. It was visible in the first rendered golden and in nothing else. The fix belonged in the shared widget (`SelectableRow.enabled`), not in this screen; the local padding that stood in for it duplicated the component's leading metric and would have drifted silently.

- Failed approaches:
  - `final SpecimenRepository r = ...; if (r is! SourceRepository) return ...;` does not promote to the intersection type at the call site here; the analyzer still refuses `r` where `SourceRepository` is wanted. A helper returning `SourceRepository?` is clearer than fighting it.
  - Writing the row with its own checkbox and tap-to-toggle before reading `selection_bar.dart`'s header. `SelectableRow` already owns that, and its rule — the body opens, only the checkbox selects — survives the case that looked like an exception: a source photograph has nothing to open, but one that is already a record does, so tap-to-toggle would make one gesture mean two things by row state, which is worse than by mode.
  - `bash verify.sh > log 2>&1; echo $?; tail log` reports `tail`'s exit code to the harness. The first run of this gate was announced as exit 0 while `verify.sh` had actually exited 1. Read the recorded status, not the notification, when the command is compound.

- Remaining follow-ups:
  - **`tests/test_sam3_runtime.py::test_sam_total_deadline_durable_unknown_and_no_retry[success]` is wall-clock flaky under load.** Line 102 asserts `time.monotonic() - started < 6`. It failed once in a full `verify.sh` run while three sessions were running their own suites on this machine, and passed 3/3 in isolation immediately after. Unrelated to this workstream. The budget is a real assertion about worker deadlines, so the fix is probably a monotonic fake rather than a larger number.
  - A source thumbnail endpoint, keyed by `(source_id, object_name, generation)`, upgrades the grid with no client change beyond swapping the placeholder for an image.
  - An exact `matching_count` under the `imported` filter needs a batched checksum lookup in the connector (`sourceChecksum: {in: [...]}`), which is the same follow-up the per-row listing cost wants. Until then that filter's select-all reaches what is loaded.

- Task: Claude Code session, backend implementation of workstreams A and B of `docs/execution/SOURCE_BROWSE_AND_RUN.md` (the design shipped as PR #56). Backend only; the client (D and E) is owned by a separate session and `apps/specimen_digitization/**` was not touched.
- Branch/worktree: `claude/eager-chatelet-20b3af` at `.claude/worktrees/eager-chatelet-20b3af`, merged up to `main` at `85b7d91` for the `.gitattributes` union driver from PR #55.
